The Food Inspector Rep., By The Pp vs Meda Bapu Reddy on 1
October, 2024
 The Honourable Sri Justice K.Surender
 Criminal Appeal No.937 Of 2013
Judgment:

entities.text: Food Inspector Rep., By The Pp vs Meda Bapu Reddy
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This criminal appeal is filed by appellant/food inspector aggrieved by the judgment, dated 09.10.2009 in C.C.No.316 of 2005 on the file of Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Chennur, wherein respondent/accused was acquitted for the offence under Section 7(i) 2(1a) (m) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act 1954 (for short "the Act"), which is punishable under Section 16(1) (a) (i) of the Act.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Chennur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard Mr. Dr.Surepalli Prashanth learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the appellant/State and perused the record.
3.
Briefly, the case of the appellant/PW1/food inspector is that he went to the premises of shop run by the accused and found about 30 kgs of Bengal gram dal in gunny bag.

Since the Bengal Gram was meant for public sale and there was suspicion that it was adulterated, PW1/food inspector purchased 1500 grams of Bengal gram dal from the above stock in cash under receipt/Ex.P2.
After purchasing the same, PW1/food inspector divided the purchased Bengal KS,J crla_937_2013 gram dal into three parts weighing 500 grams of each sample.
One of the samples was sent for the purpose of analysis by the public analyst.
The public analyst sent the report opining that the sample does not confirm to the standards of Wevilled grains and therefore adulterated.
4. Having sent the notice to the accused along with the report and after obtaining permission, the complaint was filed.
5. Learned Magistrate examined PW1/food inspector and PW2 Panch witness.
PW2 turned hostile to the prosecution case and did not support the version of PW1 that the Bengal gram dal was seized from the premises of the accused.

6. Learned Magistrate acquitted the accused on the following grounds:
a) Panch witness PW2 did not support the case of the prosecution.
b) Ex.P2/cash receipt does not reflect the name of the shop of the accused.
c) Ex.P2 was filled up by PW1 himself as admitted by him as such the document cannot be believed.
KS,J crla_937_2013 d) None of the adjacent shop keepers to the accused shop were examined.

entities.text: Food Inspector Rep., By The Pp vs Meda Bapu Reddy
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 e) The public analyst was also not examined.

7. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor would submit that there is no reason why the food inspector would launch false prosecution against the accused as the accused is stranger to him and food inspector was doing his duty.
PW1/food inspector inspected the premises and having followed the procedure, took samples and sent it for analysis.
Ex.P10/analysis report says that the samples do not conform to the standards of Wevilled grains.
8. Having gone to the record, PW1 has not collected any evidence to show that the premises, where the Bengal gram dal was seized, belongs to the accused.
Neither the ownership details of the premises were collected nor was any lease deed filed to show that the accused was running the shop.

In the absence of proving that the accused was the proprietor of Sri Virata Srinivas Kirana,
D.No.3-82/1, Gram Panchayath Road, Chinnu village, it cannot be assumed that the accused was the owner of the premises selling the Bengal gram dal, when the accused has denied the case of food inspector that accused was running the shop.

Further the findings of the learned Magistrate regarding filling up of Ex.P2/cash receipt by PW1 himself and non examination of any of the adjacent shop keepers to the shop of the accused creates any amount of doubt regarding the correctness of the complaint.
The findings cannot be found fault with it.
10. In cases of acquittal, the interference by the appellate Court can only be in compelling circumstances.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Babu v. State of Kerala 1 held as follows:

" 12. In State of Rajasthan v. Naresh @ Ram Naresh [(2009) 9 SCC 368], the Court again examined the earlier judgments of this Court and laid down that an "order of acquittal should not be lightly interfered with even if the court believes that there is some evidence pointing out the finger towards the accused."

entities.text: State of Rajasthan v. Naresh @ Ram Naresh [(2009) 9 SCC 368]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 13. In State of Uttar Pradesh v. Banne alias Baijnath & Ors. [(2009) 4 SCC 271], this Court gave certain illustrative circumstances in which the Court would be justified in interfering with a judgment of acquittal by the High Court.

entities.text: State of Uttar Pradesh v. Banne alias Baijnath & Ors. [(2009) 4 SCC 271]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Food Inspector Rep., By The Pp vs Meda Bapu Reddy
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. There are no compelling reasons put-forth by the prosecution to reverse the well reasoned judgment by the trial Court.
In the absence of proof of ownership of the premises and other discrepancies as discussed above, learned Magistrate was right in dismissing the complaint.
12. Accordingly, this appeal fails and stands dismissed.
Miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.
_ K.SURENDER, J Date: 01.10.2024
